content.text: Adam’s forward-bend test unmasks structural scoliosis.
Straight spine, level pelvis, normal curves, smooth gait.
shoulders, iliac crests & P. gluteal fold alignment
asymmetry: scoliosis, leg-length discrepancy, pelvic obliquity
Assess for scoliosis in full fwd.f lex
rib hump or uneven scapula: structural scoliosis
Erect position of head, neck & back
Presence/absence of cervical, thoracic & lumbar curves
Spinous processes, paravertebral muscles, P. S. iliac spines (usually marked by skin dimples)
hairy patch/dimple: spinal dysraphism; café-au-lait: NF
Pain radiating to leg suggests n.-root involve
- Pain radiating into buttocks, perineum & legs: into buttock/leg: nerve-root involvement
- Dimples in midline at level of gluteal cleft: asymmetric: pelvic tilt; midline: spinal dysraphism
Pain into leg w motion → neuro exam of LE
*** If these maneuvers provoke pain, particularly into leg, neuroc testing of LE is indicated
pain: facet arthropathy, stenosis, or spondylolysis
pain to side: facet; opposite: muscular
Passively raise pt leg (90’ of hip flex) -keep knee extended, then dorsiflex foot
BEST WAY TO REPROD RAD PAIN
Pain below knee at 30–70°, worse w/ dorsiflex
-tenderness or palpable spasm in this area (compresses sciatic n.against muscle):
Neuromusc dx: piriformis spasms & compress sciatic n. -> trigger deep gluteal pain, tingle, numbs radiates down back of leg,
Mimics sciatica but arises in buttock
